raw:
**Overview:**
VAS 07 and IAS 28 differ significantly in their treatment of investments held by passive investors. In VAS, passive investors typically do not have significant influence over the investee unless they hold more than 20%. Conversely, IAS 28 presumes significant influence if an investor owns at least one-fifth of the voting power.

**Comparison Table:**

| Aspect (Khía cạnh) | VAS Treatment | IFRS Treatment | Impact (Tác động) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Passive Investor Holding | No significant influence unless >20% | Significant Influence if ≥1/5 | Higher valuation under IFRS due to presumed significant influence |
| Recognition under IFRS 17 | Triggered upon initial application of IFRS 17

### Comparison

#### Year-End Translation Under VAS 10 and IAS 21

**VAS 10:**
- At the beginning of the reporting period, the foreign currency receivable is translated into local currency at the exchange rate prevailing on the day of the transaction.
- The amount remains unchanged until the end of the reporting period.
- For subsequent periods, the foreign currency receivable is translated at the exchange rate prevailing on the last day of the reporting period.

**IAS 21:**
- At the end of the reporting period, the foreign currency receivable is translated into local currency at the exchange rate prevailing on the last day of the reporting period.
- The amount remains unchanged until the next reporting period.

#### Impact

Under both standards, the foreign currency receivable is translated into local currency at the same exchange

- Sales between two subsidiaries within the reporting group are eliminated in their entirety.
- The sale price is used as the basis for determining the net profit margin of each subsidiary.

- Sales between two subsidiaries within the reporting group are combined into one item.
- The total sales amount is recognized in the consolidated income statement.
